rules.condition: When a new unilateral hemithorax opacity appears after resolution of prior ipsilateral opacity, and mediastinal shift is toward the new opacity
rules.action: Inspect for loss of lung volume (flattened diaphragm, crowding of ribs, tracheal deviation) and absence of meniscus sign to favor atelectasis over effusion

rules.condition: When mediastinal opacity obscures one heart border and tracheal deviation is present on PA CXR
rules.action: Inspect which cardiac border is silhouetted (left border loss = left mediastinal pathology; right border loss = right-sided) and confirm tracheal deviation direction—deviation away from mass side—and compare costophrenic angle blunting severity per side.
rules.limitation: Unreliable if both borders obscured or in severe cardiomegaly; requires adequate inspiration and centering.

rules.condition: When PA CXR shows enlarged central pulmonary arteries and cardiomegaly with right heart border prominence, and symptoms suggest chronic dyspnea
rules.action: Inspect lateral CXR for convex retrosternal clear space and posterior displacement of heart—signs of right ventricular hypertrophy—and exclude left-sided volume overload signs (e.g., upper lobe vessel redistribution, Kerley B lines)
rules.limitation: Unreliable in poor inspiration or scoliosis; does not differentiate etiology of PH (e.g., sarcoid vs. IPAH)

rules.condition: When a unilateral pleural-based mass is seen on PA CXR in an asymptomatic patient without asbestos exposure
rules.action: Inspect the mass–thoracic wall angle: obtuse (>90°) favors benign solitary fibrous tumor; acute (<90°) raises concern for mesothelioma or sarcoma. Confirm absence of mediastinal shift or volume loss.
rules.limitation: Requires adequate inspiratory effort and centering; unreliable if mass is obscured by cardiac or diaphragmatic shadow

rules.condition: When unilateral hyperlucency is present without obvious pleural line or mediastinal shift, and lung size appears reduced
rules.action: Inspect ipsilateral intercostal space width and hemidiaphragm position relative to contralateral side; reduced spacing + elevated diaphragm supports volume loss (e.g., Swyer-James), not hyperinflation or pneumothorax
rules.limitation: Unreliable if inspiration inadequate or diaphragm obscured by gastric air; requires comparison to contralateral side

rules.condition: When unilateral hemithorax opacity with mediastinal shift lacks volume loss signs (normal diaphragm level, normal rib spacing) and bronchovascular markings are completely absent
rules.action: Inspect for congenital absence: confirm absence of right main bronchus on CT or bronchoscopy; consider agenesis over atelectasis
rules.limitation: Rare in elderly; requires cross-sectional imaging for confirmation; cannot be diagnosed by CXR alone

rules.condition: When CXR shows bilateral nodular opacities and hilar fullness, and symmetry is ambiguous on PA view
rules.action: Inspect lateral CXR for symmetrical anterior mediastinal lymphadenopathy (prevascular nodes) and compare hilar silhouette width left vs. right on PA; exclude unilateral volume loss or pleural effusion
rules.limitation: Requires lateral view; unreliable if patient rotation or poor inspiration distorts hilar appearance

rules.condition: When bilateral symmetric coarse nodular opacities improve dramatically after immunosuppression (e.g., steroids), and cavitary or fibrotic features are absent
rules.action: Inspect for preservation of lung volumes and absence of traction bronchiectasis or reticulation on follow-up to distinguish acute hemorrhage resolution from chronic granulomatous/fibrotic disease regression
rules.limitation: Requires adequate inspiration and comparable projection; unreliable if follow-up is CT misinterpreted as CXR

rules.condition: When CXR shows a new or enlarging cavitary lesion in the upper lobe with irregular thick wall (>15 mm) and adjacent soft-tissue opacity, and symptoms are subacute
rules.action: Inspect for mass effect (mediastinal shift, hilum displacement), wall thickness on magnified view, and absence of satellite nodules; consider malignancy over TB
rules.limitation: Unreliable if image quality poor or no prior imaging for comparison

rules.condition: When CXR shows diffuse interstitial opacities and fissural thickening in a patient with systemic symptoms, and cardiac silhouette appears borderline enlarged on PA view
rules.action: Quantify cardiothoracic ratio (max transverse cardiac width / inner thoracic diameter); if ≥0.52, consider cardiomegaly and evaluate for pulmonary vascular redistribution or right heart enlargement signs
rules.limitation: Inadequate inspiration inflates CT ratio; scoliosis distorts measurements

rules.limitation: Unreliable if lateral view is rotated or overpenetrated; does not distinguish tumor from consolidation without clinical context

rules.limitation: Requires visible aortic calcification; unreliable in young patients or non-calcified aorta

rules.condition: When mediastinal lymphadenopathy and tracheal deviation worsen on CXR *after* ART initiation in an HIV+ patient
rules.action: Inspect serial CXRs for interval increase in mediastinal opacity width (>1 cm) and direction of tracheal shift (away from enlarged nodes); correlate with ART start date if available
rules.limitation: Requires at least two temporally spaced CXRs; unreliable if poor technique or non-standard projection

rules.condition: When a cystic-appearing lucency abuts the hilum on initial CXR and appears absent on follow-up, but diagnosis hinges on persistence vs resolution
rules.action: Overlay or align images by bony landmarks (e.g., carina, 6th rib) and inspect for residual thin-walled lucency or subtle interface at exact prior location; if uncertain, request CT.
rules.limitation: Fails if images not same projection or magnification; cannot substitute for CT in equivocal cases

rules.condition: When a serpentine tubular opacity is seen in the medial right lung on PA CXR with ipsilateral volume loss elsewhere
rules.action: Inspect its trajectory on lateral view: if it descends posteriorly along the right heart border toward the diaphragm without air lucency and tapers, suspect anomalous pulmonary vein; confirm absence of air column and compare to expected bronchial/arterial courses
rules.limitation: Cannot differentiate small aneurysms or vascular malformations without contrast; unreliable if poor inspiration or rotation

rules.condition: When evaluating CXR for sarcoidosis staging and upper-zone nodularity is present with bilateral hilar fullness
rules.action: Compare nodule density in upper vs. lower lung zones using the carina as midpoint; verify symmetry of hilar silhouette width on PA and anterior mediastinal density on lateral view
rules.limitation: Unreliable if poor inspiration causes apparent lower-zone crowding or if rotation mimics unilateral adenopathy

rules.condition: When a well-defined anterior mediastinal opacity is seen on PA and LL CXR without air lucencies or tracheal deviation
rules.action: Inspect lateral view for smooth, non-lobulated contour abutting sternum and lack of double bronchial wall sign; if present, favor benign mass (e.g., lipoma) over pneumomediastinum
rules.limitation: Cannot exclude low-density sarcoma or thymoma without CT; unreliable if overpenetrated or poor LL projection

rules.condition: When a peripheral, well-circumscribed opacity is seen on PA CXR without effusion or volume loss
rules.action: Evaluate lateral view for obtuse angle with chest wall and cortical rib changes; if both present, favor benign pleural neoplasm (e.g., solitary fibrous tumor)
rules.limitation: Unreliable if lateral view is rotated or obscured by overlying structures

rules.condition: When two PA CXRs show subtle linear mediastinal lucencies and diagnosis hinges on stability vs progression of pneumomediastinum
rules.action: Overlay images using bony landmarks (carina, 6th rib); inspect for change in length/width of lucencies paralleling trachea/bronchi; exclude pleural line, subdiaphragmatic gas, and pericardial halo
rules.limitation: Requires same projection and magnification; unreliable if poor inspiration or rotation differs >5°

rules.condition: In immunocompromised patients with solitary/multiple pulmonary nodules and no endemic exposure, when CT shows peripheral, solid, non-cavitary nodules ≥1 cm without calcification
rules.action: Inspect for subtle surrounding ground-glass halo or adjacent pleural tag; if present, prioritize fungal infection (e.g., blastomycosis) over PTLD pending microbiologic confirmation
rules.limitation: Halo may be absent in early or treated disease; unreliable without thin-section CT and window optimization

rules.condition: When left heart border is obscured AND mediastinal widening AND contralateral (right) mediastinal shift are present on PA CXR
rules.action: Inspect lateral CXR for anterior mediastinal opacity overlapping cardiac silhouette from thoracic inlet downward; if present, prioritize thymic malignancy (e.g., T-ALL) in young patients
rules.limitation: Does not apply if patient is adult or if opacity is posterior (e.g., neurogenic tumor); requires adequate lateral projection

rules.condition: When CT shows multiple thin-walled cavitary nodules and clinical history includes laryngeal/supraglottic papillomatous lesion
rules.action: Inspect nodule wall thickness on high-resolution window (thin <2 mm) and exclude upper-lobe predominance or nodular bronchiectasis; if confirmed, prioritize RRP over PLCH/GPA
rules.limitation: Fails if nodules are too small to measure wall or if prior imaging shows evolution toward solid nodules

rules.condition: When a well-circumscribed unilateral opacity abuts the thoracic wall on PA CXR and appears to displace lung without infiltrating it
rules.action: Measure the lesion–chest wall angle: obtuse (>90°) supports benign extrapleural origin (e.g., solitary fibrous tumor); acute (<90°) warrants concern for malignancy or rib involvement
rules.limitation: Unreliable if lesion is obscured by cardiac shadow, diaphragm, or poor inspiration; confirm with lateral view or CT if ambiguous

evicted_rule.condition: When bilateral micronodules are stable over years on CXR and granulomatous disease is considered, but no hilar adenopathy or upper-lobe predominance is seen
evicted_rule.action: Inspect CT for airway-centered nodules, mosaic attenuation, and absence of calcified granulomas; if CT unavailable, prioritize clinical symptoms (chronic cough/wheeze) and serum chromogranin A
evicted_rule.limitation: CXR alone cannot confirm DIPNECH; rule not applicable if CT shows classic sarcoid or TB pattern

evicted_rule.condition: When CT shows multiple discrete hyperdense pulmonary nodules with lower lobe predominance and no upper lobe involvement
evicted_rule.action: Inspect bone-window CT slices to confirm intrinsic calcification (Hounsfield >200 HU) and exclude endobronchial or vascular causes by checking for air bronchograms or vessel continuity
evicted_rule.limitation: May fail in early ossification before full calcification; unreliable if motion artifact or metal streaks obscure density measurement

evicted_rule.condition: When bilateral peripheral airspace consolidations lack eosinophilia clues and patient has risk factors for aspiration (e.g., GERD, neurologic impairment, oral lipid use)
evicted_rule.action: Inspect for subtle basilar accentuation and air bronchograms within opacities; prioritize CT for fat attenuation (-10 to -100 HU) if suspicion remains
evicted_rule.limitation: CXR cannot confirm fat density; requires CT or history for definitive distinction from CEP

evicted_rule.condition: In post-lobectomy CXRs showing new or worsening ipsilateral opacification, when lobar identity is ambiguous due to absent fissures
evicted_rule.action: Inspect for focal convex opacity with medial/ventral displacement relative to prior image and absence of expected volume loss—suggesting torsion rather than atelectasis or fluid
evicted_rule.limitation: Fails if overpenetration obscures lobar contours; does not distinguish torsion from mucus plugging with air trapping without clinical correlation

evicted_rule.condition: When CXR shows a new unilateral upper/mid-lung opacity in a patient with electrical injury and no trauma/surgery, and the opacity abuts the hilum without diaphragmatic silhouetting
evicted_rule.action: Inspect for loss of hilar silhouette (silhouette sign) and absence of meniscus or visceral pleural line; assess for air bronchograms to favor consolidation over atelectasis or effusion
evicted_rule.limitation: Fails if overpenetration obscures subtle opacities or if lateral view unavailable; cannot distinguish infection from thermal injury without clinical context

evicted_rule.condition: When a well-circumscribed thoracic mass lacks acute angles at lung interface on PA CXR
evicted_rule.action: Inspect lateral CXR for posterior location relative to cardiac silhouette and spine; obtuse angles + posterior position strongly favor extrapulmonary benign tumor (e.g., schwannoma)
evicted_rule.limitation: Unreliable if breast tissue or poor inspiration obscures posterior structures; does not distinguish schwannoma from other posterior neurogenic tumors

evicted_rule.condition: When unilateral lung opacification shows air bronchograms extending from apex to base on PA CXR and lateral view confirms anterior–posterior involvement without volume loss
evicted_rule.action: Inspect for continuity of opacification across all three lobes and absence of silhouetting of hemidiaphragm or hilum that would suggest lobar collapse; confirm no tracheal deviation
evicted_rule.limitation: Fails if overpenetration masks subtle air bronchograms or if prior surgery/atelectasis confounds lobar boundaries

evicted_rule.condition: When assessing for neuroblastic tumor recurrence on CXR and the clinical concern is subclavicular or paravertebral region
evicted_rule.action: Inspect the paravertebral stripe bilaterally for new soft-tissue density with stippled or coarse calcifications; compare to prior studies if available
evicted_rule.limitation: Calcifications may be invisible on CXR if <2 mm or obscured by overlying structures; CT required for confirmation

evicted_rule.condition: When recurrent lobar consolidation resolves completely on follow-up CXR but reappears at identical location in a non-smoker or young patient (<50), and no systemic symptoms suggest malignancy
evicted_rule.action: Inspect the resolved region on intermediate CXR for faint persistent linear or nodular density along bronchus; if present, suspect benign endobronchial tumor (e.g., fibrolipoma) and recommend CT with bronchial window
evicted_rule.limitation: Unreliable in smokers >45 or with weight loss/hemoptysis; cannot exclude carcinoma without CT

evicted_rule.condition: When acute chest pain and supraclavicular crepitus are present and CXR appears normal or shows only subtle lucencies near clavicles
evicted_rule.action: Inspect central bronchi on PA CXR for paired linear lucencies (inner + outer wall outline); confirm they follow bronchial course without branching and are not vascular
evicted_rule.limitation: May be missed in poor inspiration or overpenetrated films; requires comparison with prior imaging if available

evicted_rule.condition: When difficult intubation is reported and lateral neck CXR is available
evicted_rule.action: Inspect for radiopaque material in the oropharynx (anterior to C3–C4, superior to vocal cords); if present, prioritize foreign body over pleural pathology
evicted_rule.limitation: Fails if foreign body is radiolucent or obscured by dental hardware; requires adequate lateral projection

evicted_rule.condition: When CXR shows unilateral volume loss with mediastinal shift and contralateral hyperlucency but no pleural line or effusion signs
evicted_rule.action: Inspect axial CT at carina level for presence/absence of ipsilateral main pulmonary artery; absence confirms agenesis
evicted_rule.limitation: Not applicable if only CXR available; requires contrast-enhanced CT for reliable vessel visualization

evicted_rule.condition: When a well-defined, round, non-cavitating parenchymal opacity is seen in the lower lobe of an adult with acute respiratory symptoms but no air-fluid level on lateral CXR
evicted_rule.action: Inspect for smooth, thin wall and absence of perilesional consolidation; consider hydatid cyst especially if endemic exposure possible
evicted_rule.limitation: Cannot exclude early abscess or tumor without CT; acute symptoms reduce likelihood but do not rule out hydatid rupture

evicted_rule.condition: When bilateral patchy opacities are present and right heart border is obscured on PA CXR
evicted_rule.action: Inspect lateral CXR for anterior-inferior opacity overlapping cardiac silhouette and diaphragm dome to localize to right middle lobe; correlate with perihilar predominance
evicted_rule.limitation: Unreliable if lateral view is rotated or inspiration inadequate; does not confirm etiology without immune status

evicted_rule.condition: When reticular opacities appear asymmetric in lower zones on PA CXR and hyperlucency is suspected in upper zones
evicted_rule.action: Quantify lower-zone reticulation by counting visible interstitial lines per cm² in each hemithorax at mid-lung field; assess upper-zone hyperlucency by measuring intercostal space width at T3–T5 and comparing vascular tapering from hilum to periphery bilaterally
evicted_rule.limitation: Requires adequate inspiration and absence of overpenetration; unreliable if diaphragm not fully visualized

evicted_rule.condition: When axial CT shows a tubular vessel left of the aortic arch near the left atrium and pulmonary artery, with absent left upper pulmonary vein opacification
evicted_rule.action: Inspect for continuity from left pulmonary veins to this vessel and trace its superior course toward the left brachiocephalic vein confluence
evicted_rule.limitation: Requires contrast-enhanced venous-phase imaging; unreliable in non-contrast or arterial-phase scans

evicted_rule.condition: When PA CXR shows a solitary opacity silhouetting the right hemidiaphragm but sparing the right heart border
evicted_rule.action: Inspect lateral CXR for opacity position relative to spine: if posterior to vertebral bodies and overlapping diaphragm dome, localize to posterior right lower lobe; assess margin smoothness and absence of cavitation/calcification
evicted_rule.limitation: Unreliable if lateral view is rotated or underpenetrated; does not differentiate benign from malignant without additional features

evicted_rule.condition: When bilateral alveolar opacities show lower/mid-zone predominance with upper-sparing on PA CXR and anterior-inferior opacity overlaps cardiac silhouette on lateral view
evicted_rule.action: Inspect for preserved apical lucency and absence of upper-lobe vascular redistribution or Kerley lines; if present, favor PAP over cardiogenic edema or ARDS
evicted_rule.limitation: Cannot exclude infection or hemorrhage without clinical context; unreliable if inspiration inadequate or rotation present

evicted_rule.condition: When a right lower lung opacity abuts the right heart border on PA CXR but the costophrenic angle remains sharp and no air bronchogram is seen
evicted_rule.action: Inspect lateral CXR for anterior soft-tissue density overlapping the cardiac silhouette and diaphragmatic dome; if present with depressed sternum and no air lucency, favor chest wall projection
evicted_rule.limitation: Unreliable if lateral view is rotated, overpenetrated, or lacks sternum visualization

evicted_rule.condition: When a thoracic mass is clinically suspected but not evident on PA CXR, especially with unilateral symptoms
evicted_rule.action: Inspect lateral CXR or oblique views for dorsolateral rib widening, soft-tissue density abutting the chest wall without pleural separation, particularly at levels T2–T4
evicted_rule.limitation: PA-only CXR insufficient; requires orthogonal imaging to exclude extrapleural or chest-wall masses

evicted_rule.condition: When CXR shows a non-linear, lobulated opacity in the right lower zone with indistinct margins and possible internal lucency on magnified view
evicted_rule.action: Inspect for trefoil (trilobed/branching) morphology and absence of volume loss signs (e.g., diaphragmatic elevation, mediastinal shift); if present, consider bronchial atresia
evicted_rule.limitation: Requires high-resolution magnified view; unreliable if opacity overlaps heart border without lateral confirmation
